column1: # docs/inspection.md §18.3 count ratchet — see tools/count-ratchet.sh
# id<TAB>count.  A count may FALL freely; raising one is a deliberate act.
# 2026-10-01: 8.1.8 +2 and 10.7 +3 are CORPUS GROWTH, not drift — both are the
# pre-existing style of bin/qwen-memory-index-patch.sh (two >120-char lines, three
# `echo … >&2` sites), a script that lived only as an unversioned ~/.local/bin copy
# until it was tracked here.  Deliberate re-baseline for ONE newly added file.
# (Restored by hand after `--update`: the tool rewrites the file without comments.)
# 2026-10-01 (second re-baseline, same day): every rise below is the PRE-EXISTING
# style of code that became TRACKED, not new drift — six files moved in from loose
# ~/.local/bin copies (autotune-rows.sh, bench-rows.sh, gpu-passthrough-check.sh,
# so, xo, serve) plus bin/heavy-job, which is new.  Corpus 81 -> 88 files.
# Not counted here: bin/heavy-job's own single `[ … ]`, which was changed to
# `[[ … ]]` instead — the counter's ask — when it was written.
# 2026-10-01 (third re-baseline, same day): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift.  Two files were
# tracked in from loose ~/.local/bin copies — bin/qwen-guard-patch.sh and
# bin/qwen-guard-selfheal.sh — with their own edits kept comment-only, so every counter
# they raise is pre-existing style.  Contributions measured by running the counters over
# 2026-10-01 (fourth re-baseline, same day): what the TRACKED corpus actually holds.
# d1df5ce9 tracked ONE new shell file, bin/qwen-guard-selfheal.sh; measured with this
# tool's own counters over that file alone it raises 4.2.4 +1 and 6.7 +4.  Corpus
# 89 -> 90.  The third block above counted bin/qwen-guard-patch.sh as tracked too, but
# it is still UNTRACKED, so its 8.1.8 +18 / 9.5 +2 / 10.4 +1 / 10.7 +10 are absent from
# this corpus — which is why those four counts sit BELOW the third block's numbers.
# 8.1.8's 272 also carries +2 from another lane's uncommitted scripts/09d-oc-agents.sh
# edit, which the working-tree ratchet sees (that count falls to 270 if the edit is not
# committed).  Deliberate re-baseline: corpus growth, not drift.
# 2026-10-01 (fifth re-baseline, same day): bin/qwen-guard-patch.sh is now TRACKED
# (commit 7ce7ae82), so the third block's numbers are realised and the fourth block's
# "still UNTRACKED" caveat is retired.  Corpus 90 -> 91.  Measured contributions from
# 10.7 171 -> 181 (+10); 6.7 is UNCHANGED at 57, so the third block's "6.7 +2" was not
# borne out (measured, not assumed).  The +2 the fourth block attributed to the
# uncommitted scripts/09d-oc-agents.sh edit is now committed (2f1b5a1d) and sits inside
# the 272 this rises from.  Deliberate re-baseline: corpus growth, not drift.
# 2026-10-02 (sixth re-baseline): NOT corpus growth — a deliberate style fix in
# scripts/09e-oc-health.sh.  Item 10.7 rose 181 -> 182 because the five `|| true`
# swallow sites now report their failure on stderr, routed through ONE helper
# (__oc_note) instead of five ad-hoc redirects.  The counter counts the helper's own
# single write and cannot express "a helper rather than ad-hoc", which is exactly what
# this item asks for — so the +1 is the cost of complying, not drift.  8.1.8 fell
# 290 -> 289 and 6.7 fell 57 -> 56 as side effects of the same edit (a long multi-line
# jq call re-wrapped, one ad-hoc stderr site removed).  Measured with this tool's own
# counters; no other count moved.
# 2026-10-02 (seventh re-baseline): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift - ONE new shell file,
# bin/qwen-memory-style-patch.sh (commit 8f157a47). Measured with this tool's OWN counters
# over that file ALONE: 8.1.8 +1 (one 190-char line), 10.7 +3 (three >&2 sites); every other
# counter 0 there. The same commit's edit to bin/qwen-guard-selfheal.sh converted two
# `[ -x ... ]` tests to `[[ -x ... ]]` (item 6.7's ask), so 6.7 FELL 56 -> 54 - recorded
# because a fall is informational and the row must match reality.
# Hand-edited, NOT --update, which rewrites this file as header+rows and strips these comments:
# 6.7 56->54, 8.1.8 289->290, 10.7 182->185; the other six rows are unchanged.
# 2026-10-02 (eighth re-baseline): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift - the NAS (butler) tooling is
# mirrored into this repo for the first time (nas/butler/, commit 49c1abe2: 16 shell files
# that had lived only on /mnt/HD/HD_a2/butler). Every rise below is the PRE-EXISTING style
# of that foreign code, not new drift: 6.7 +23 (`[ ... ]` instead of `[[ ... ]]`), 8.1.8 +6
# (lines over 120 characters), 9.5 +17 (functions with no comment directly above - a
# convention that codebase never had), 10.7 +5 (hand-written `>&2` on echo/printf). Corpus
# 92 -> 108 files. Nothing was relaxed: the mirrored scripts are byte-identical to the NAS
# except the two gate fixes recorded in nas/butler/README.md, and tools/lint.sh's whole-tree
# scope still excludes nas/ - this row set records knowledge, not a lowered gate.
# 2026-10-02 (ninth re-baseline): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift - TWO new shell tools land with
# the gitleaks secret scanner (card a7383ea0): tools/install-gitleaks.sh and
# tools/secret-scan.sh. Measured with this tool's OWN counters over those two files ALONE:
# 9.7 +4 (four literal `exit 2` returns) and 10.7 +5 (five hand-written `>&2` sites); they
# contribute 0 to 6.7 / 8.1.8 / 9.5 / 10.4. Corpus 107 -> 109 files. Hand-edited, NOT
# --update (which rewrites this file as header+rows and strips these comments):
# 9.7 56->60, 10.7 190->195. Also recorded, as FALLS from elsewhere in the tree
# (informational; they are not from the two new files): 8.1.8 296->294, 9.5 124->121.
# 2026-10-04 (tenth re-baseline): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift - ONE new shell tool lands with the
# bats pin (card 93909ea5): tools/install-bats.sh. Over that file ALONE: 10.7 +3 (three
# hand-written `>&2` sites) and 0 to 6.7 / 8.1.8 / 9.5 / 10.4. Corpus 110 -> 111 files. Applied
# with `tools/count-ratchet.sh --update`, which preserved the comment blocks above on this run:
# 10.4 50->49) are the tree's own, not from the new file.
